own_solution.law: RC charging: V_C(t) = E (1 - exp(-t/RC)), tau = 0.1 s
assumptions: capacitor initially uncharged (listed by the authors but not stated in the problem)
ideal battery and wires, no leakage

defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: The authors' own assumption list needs 'the capacitor is initially uncharged', but the problem text never states it, and any initial charge changes V_C(80 ms).

counterexamples: Initial capacitor voltage 5 V gives V_C(80 ms) = 12 - 7 e^-0.8 = 8.855 V, not 6.608 V.
notes: All certified numbers check: base 12(1-e^-0.8)=6.60805 V; extra resistor 1/2/5 kOhm gives tau 0.12/0.14/0.20 s and 5.839/5.223/3.956 V. K regime q > t holds for all listed values 300/500/1000 ms (all > 80 ms). D sentences are genuinely disconnected; minimal pairs (T401C-TFDE0, T8B5D-T1D0A) keep the same 2 kOhm value and differ only in attachment. The only defect is the unstated initial condition, which agrees with my pass 1. 'Broken again' in T8E15 is slightly awkward wording (no prior break), not a defect of the physics.
